releases.narrativeDevelopment: Gideon's third pilot beat. Sloane reads Kai's note: "Celestine has a vision she never built. She'll never ask. I'm asking." Gideon: "He can't ask. He has no standing. releases.title: Through the Door

releases.setting: Sloane's office at Halcyon House, morning; then the Crescent Room during a weekday band rehearsal.

openingHook.text: Royce comes back through the proper door, with a referral card from Mr. Daniels, the jazz-club owner he once worked for as a bar-back.
openingHook.derivation: First beat of WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS in the approved Option A map

releases.narrativeDevelopment: - Royce comes back through the proper door, with a referral card from Mr. Daniels, the jazz-club owner he once worked for as a bar-back. Gideon shows him in without comment. - The request, in one breath: the Crescent Room Orchestra for the Salon's tenth anniversary. Clarence Moody has refused him four times, because the orchestra only plays rooms where phones stay down. - His offering: the first devices-down hour in the Salon's history, and the band keeps every right to its music. "You want my help?" "I want the best. Don't let it go to your head." Sloane takes the case and enjoys it far too much. - At the Crescent Room, Sloane doesn't sell Royce. She tells Clarence what the hour would mean: two hundred young people hearing a big band with nothing in their hands. Clarence: "First hour, no phones. And he dances the first number." "He doesn't dance." "Then he doesn't get the band."
releases.characterPurpose: Starts the request engine in the first arc, with a rival as the patron: Sloane facilitates for someone she competes with.
releases.payoff: A viewer learns the mechanics in a minute: sponsor, request, offering, and who decides. Plants Clarence's no-phones rule (S1-35, S1-74) and the Salon's anniversary (S1-28).
releases.endingTransition: Royce, on the phone, after a long pause: "Fine. Find me a teacher." Sloane hangs up and laughs out loud.

releases.narrativeDevelopment: Sloane tells Gideon first: "I think this Grand Exchange is my last. As the one who decides." Gideon takes it with dry grace: "Last as in last, or last as in you'll change your mind by spring?" "I'm not leaving. I'll still host. I'll still take the impossible requests. I just don't want my opinion of someone to be their whole life anymore." Gideon: "And what do you want?" Sloane: "Dessert." He lets it go; he has known her long enough to hear a door close. releases.narrativeDevelopment: - Sloane pauses new personal sponsorships, which is visible to every sponsor in the network. A club owner calls, puzzled: "You paused? You never pause." She charms her way off the phone ("I'm learning to rest. Don't tell anyone, it's embarrassing"), then buys too many oranges. - The fruit seller calls after her: "Lockwood! Tell your father he owes me a dance." Then she sets something else on the scale: a brass Pledge token, worn smooth, stamped 1986. Freeze-frame: "MAVIS ODOM: Sells oranges. Forgets nothing. Forgives most things." - The night Nadine was born, Mavis drove Richard and his wife to the hospital in her fruit truck. Richard pledged her one dance, at a time of her choosing. She's choosing now. - Sloane can't make her father dance. She can deliver a Recall, and she takes the token like a jewel. - On the walk home, oranges in both arms, she decides a debt that old deserves a room, not a phone call. She rings the Crescent Room's bandleader: "Clarence. I need your Saturday."

releases.endingTransition: Mavis: "Saturday after next. The Crescent Room. Tell him to stretch." Sloane promises she will.

openingHook.text: Sloane and Tina argue happily across the racks.
openingHook.derivation: First beat of WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS in the approved Option A map

releases.narrativeDevelopment: - Sloane and Tina argue happily across the racks. Sloane wears a 1980s cropped jacket over a slip dress; Tina wears four thousand dollars of somebody's new collection. Freeze-frame: "TINA GRANDISON: Edits the city's best fashion magazine. Has never once admitted I was right about shoulders." - Tina, almost shy, makes a request. For two years a woman on her morning Number 9 bus has dressed better than anything in her pages. Tina doesn't know her name. In this city you don't photograph a stranger and you don't follow one home. "I want to meet her. I'll put her on the cover." - Sloane asks for details. Hand-rolled lapels, and a flash of wax-print lining inside every cuff. Sloane goes still: she knows that finish. It's taught in one place, a church sewing circle off Ferry Street. - She doesn't need the woman's name. She has Tina write her letter on Relay paper, which stays blank for everyone except the person it's meant for.
releases.characterPurpose: Sloane's fashion knowledge becomes her facilitator's skill. A friend becomes a patron.
releases.payoff: Lived-in fashion (vintage shopping, strong opinions, an argument about shoulders) that is also the start of an exchange. The Relay paper is experienced before it's explained.
releases.endingTransition: The card goes blank in Tina's hand. Tina: "Did it just—" Sloane: "It's not ours anymore."

Nadine, mid-hand, doesn't look up: "You came to a hospital in opera gloves." Sloane: "Do me a favour. I'll owe you." Nadine: "You don't owe me. You ask me. Properly."
